query_snapshot: For hydrogen peroxide solution from 30 to 70 percent, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour group and which in its 4-hour group?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- For hydrogen peroxide (solution 30%–70%), the archived NIOSH A–Z table lists the following barriers in its >8 hours (8-hour) group: Butyl rubber, Natural rubber, Nitrile rubber, PE, Viton, CPF3, Responder, Tychem. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- For hydrogen peroxide (solution 30%–70%), the archived NIOSH A–Z table lists the following barriers in its >4 hours (4-hour) group: PVC, PE/EVAL (i.e., at least 4 but less than 8 hours resistance). [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- NIOSH’s table defines the barrier categories such that ">8 hours" indicates resistance to chemical breakthrough during an 8-hour test (permeation did not exceed 1.0 µg/cm2/min during the 8-hour test) and "4 hr" indicates at least 4 but less than 8 hours of resistance. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
